title: Interfacility transfer: intracerebral haemorrhage
stem: Resus. Mr Yip, 60, has sudden left-sided weakness. GCS 11 (E3V3M5). Your hospital has no neurosurgery; the tertiary centre has accepted him. Review the CT, prepare him for transfer and manage problems on the way.
notes:
Checked against the Association of Anaesthetists interhospital transfer guideline (2019), the Intensive Care Society transfer guidance (2019), NICE NG128 stroke (2019, updated 2022), AHA/ASA spontaneous ICH guideline (2022), and ATLS 10th.

Preparation (your 8 points match): communication (patient/family, receiving team, transport team, ambulance), documentation, consent, equipment/kit (monitoring, suction, oxygen with reserve, drugs pre-drawn and labelled), pre-transport assessment and stabilisation (secure airway if GCS ≤8, falling GCS, or airway at risk; two IV lines; tubes and lines secured), appropriate escort (critical → doctor plus nurse). ICH specifics: SBP target 130–140 within an hour if presenting within 6 hours with SBP 150–220 (NICE; AHA 140, avoid under 130), reverse anticoagulation, head up 30°, glucose normal, treat seizures. Deterioration uses your REST approach (Recognise, Evaluate, Support, Transport); for the intubated patient, DOPES.

Differences from your notes: (1) needle decompression — your notes say 2nd ICS midclavicular; ATLS 10th recommends the 4th/5th ICS just anterior to the mid-axillary line in adults (2nd ICS MCL for children). (2) 'Reintubation not recommended' in the ambulance: better to say ventilate with a bag-mask or supraglottic airway first and reintubate only if needed and safe (stop the vehicle).

steps.label: CT and bloods
steps.hint: Describe the CT; check clotting and glucose.

Imaging.r: Hyperdense haematoma in the right basal ganglia/thalamus with blood in the lateral ventricle.
Imaging.mark: Describes the right deep ICH with intraventricular extension

steps.label: Stabilise
steps.hint: Lower SBP to 130–140, head up 30°, airway decision, lines.

opts.t: Head up 30°, two IV lines, all secured
Airway: GCS 11 and protecting — no intubation now, but escort able to intubate; RSI drugs pre-drawn and labelled

opts.r: Avoid SBP under 130; risks cerebral hypoperfusion.

steps.label: Prepare the transfer
steps.hint: Communication, documentation, consent, equipment, pre-transport check, escort level.

opts.t: Communicate: family, receiving neurosurgeon, transport team, ambulance; ETA agreed
Document condition, treatment, vital signs and plan; copy of CT and notes
Explain risks and benefits to family; consent
Transport kit: monitor, suction, oxygen enough for twice the journey, drugs
Critical patient: escorted by a doctor and a nurse
Send him with the porter; he is talking
opts.r: GCS 11 with ICH is critical and may deteriorate.

steps.label: GCS drops en route
steps.hint: GCS 7, right pupil dilating. REST: recognise, evaluate ABC and pupils and glucose, support (airway), tell the receiving team.

opts.t: Recognise: GCS 7, right pupil dilated, HR falling
Support: stop the ambulance; RSI with pre-drawn drugs; ETCO2 4.5–5
Transport: inform the receiving team; consider hypertonic saline or mannitol per neurosurgeon

steps.label: SpO2 falls to 84%
steps.hint: DOPES: displacement, obstruction, pneumothorax, equipment, stacking.

DOPES.t: Displacement: tube mark, ETCO2 trace, bilateral air entry
DOPES.r: Tube at 22 cm, trace present, equal air entry.

wrong: 2nd ICS in the midclavicular line, for adults and children
7th ICS in the posterior axillary line

qs.a: GCS ≤8, falling GCS, or airway at risk
wrong: Every intracerebral haemorrhage, whatever the GCS

qs.a: At least twice the expected need
wrong: Half the expected need, plus a spare

badge.name: Safe Passage
badge.flavor: Stabilise before you go. Twice the oxygen. REST, then DOPES.

options: A single nurse with an airway kit
A porter and a healthcare assistant
Half the calculated need, plus a spare
Reverse with PCC and vitamin K
Add aspirin 300 mg for the stroke
